title: 3Sum With Multiplicity
summary: For an integer array arr and a target integer, count the number of unique triplets (i, j, k) where i < j < k and arr[i] + arr[j] + arr[k] equals the target.
statement: For an integer array arr and a target integer, count the number of unique triplets (i, j, k) where i < j < k and arr[i] + arr[j] + arr[k] equals the target. The result should be given modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Count index triples i<j<k whose values sum to target.
reference_solution:
def three_sum_multiplicity(arr, target):
 from collections import Counter
 count=Counter(arr);values=sorted(count);answer=0
 for i,x in enumerate(values):
  for y in values[i:]:
   z=target-x-y
   if z<y or z not in count:continue
   if x==y==z:answer+=count[x]*(count[x]-1)*(count[x]-2)//6
   elif x==y:answer+=count[x]*(count[x]-1)//2*count[z]
   elif y==z:answer+=count[x]*count[y]*(count[y]-1)//2
   else:answer+=count[x]*count[y]*count[z]
 return answer%1000000007
